```{r setup, include=FALSE}
  "British Indian Ocean Territory" = "IOT",
  "Cabo Verde" = "CPV",
  "Comoros" = "COM",
  "Madagascar" = "MDG",
  "Mauritius" = "MUS",

fmt_eu_coord <- function (x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(x), 2L), nsmall = 2L, trim = TRUE)
  gsub("\\.", ",", s)
}

fmt_era_yr <- function (y) {
  yi <- as.integer(y)
  if (yi < 0L) paste0(abs(yi), "BC") else if (yi == 0L) "1AD" else paste0(yi, "AD")
}

interp_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- vals[ord]
  if (yr_num < yrs[1] || yr_num > yrs[length(yrs)]) return(NA_real_)
  idx <- which(yrs == yr_num)
  if (length(idx) > 0L) return(vals[idx[1]])
  stats::approx(x = yrs, y = vals, xout = yr_num, method = "linear")$y
}

fmt_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr_num)
  if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}

fmt_site_peak <- function (e) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return("-")
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  i_pk <- which.max(vals)
  paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(vals[i_pk]), " (", fmt_era_yr(yrs[i_pk]), ")")
}

  "merina_central_highlands",
  "betsileo_southern_highlands",
  "betsimisaraka_east_madagascar",
  "antandroy_mahafaly_south_mdg",

  "seychelles_chagos_wio"
)

entry_sub_ids <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
  s <- subregion_lookup[[e$key]]
  if (is.null(s)) "merina_central_highlands" else s
}, character(1))

zone_entries <- setNames(lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- all_entries[entry_sub_ids == sid]
  pks <- vapply(sub, function (e) max(as.numeric(unlist(e$population))), numeric(1))
  sub[order(-pks, vapply(sub, function (e) e$name, character(1)))]
}), subregion_order)

build_gazetteer_df <- function (sub_list) {
  rows <- lapply(sub_list, function (e) {
    iso_code <- iso3_map[[as.character(e$country)]]
    if (is.null(iso_code)) iso_code <- toupper(substr(as.character(e$country), 1L, 3L))
    loc_str <- paste0(iso_code, ": ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]]))
    data.frame(
      Settlement = as.character(e$name),
      Location = loc_str,
      `1100AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1100),
      `1400AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1400),
      `1700AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1700),
      `1810AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1810),
      `1890AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1890),
      Peak = fmt_site_peak(e),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(df) <- NULL
  df
}

n_excluded <- as.integer(summary_cache$wave_saturation_stats$ledger_excluded)
n_candidates <- length(all_entries) + n_excluded
bench_nums <- c(1100, 1400, 1700, 1810, 1890)
bench_keys <- as.character(bench_nums)
n_active <- setNames(
  vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, yr)), logical(1))), integer(1)),
  bench_keys
)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates and multi-period population series for `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements across ten island jurisdictions in the western Indian Ocean and African Atlantic between 500BC and 1895AD. Screened from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidate archaeological sites, Malagasy royal hilltops, Comorian stone towns and European colonial ports (`r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate alias removed), the entries span ten sub-regions across Madagascar, Mauritius, Réunion, Comoros, Mayotte, Cabo Verde, São Tomé e Príncipe, Seychelles, Saint Helena and the Chagos Archipelago. Active interpolated sites rise from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1100"]], 0L)` mediaeval centres at 1100AD and `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1400"]], 0L)` at 1400AD to `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1700"]], 0L)` at 1700AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1810"]], 0L)` at 1810AD and `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1890"]], 0L)` at 1890AD, tracing urban development from Dembéni and Mahilaka to Antananarivo (75k peak), Port-Louis (74,5k), Saint-Denis (36,1k), Saint-Pierre (27,8k), Saint-Paul (24,9k), Mindelo (6,24k), São Tomé (6,85k) and Victoria (6,24k).

# Background

Island urbanism around Africa developed along two contrasting archival tracks. On Madagascar and the Comoros, early Austronesian and Swahili-Bantu mariners built stone mosques, fortified hilltop enclosures and coastal entrepots centuries before European arrival [@Beaujard2007EastAfricaMadagascar; @ICM2020MadagascarAtlas]. Across the uninhabited Mascarenes, Seychelles, Chagos, Cabo Verde, São Tomé e Príncipe and Saint Helena, permanent settlement began only after 1460AD with Portuguese, Dutch, French and British colonial ports, slave-worked estates and nineteenth-century coaling stations [@Seibert2014CrioulizacaoCabo; @Allen1999SlavesFreedmen; @Oliver1950TheVoyage]. Uniting archaeological surveys with French East India Company returns, British colonial censuses and Lusophone *ultramar* registers yields a consistent settlement ledger across `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` chronological observations.

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Sub-Regional Partition

Candidate localities were screened from regional archaeological inventories, nineteenth-century geographical monographs and colonial statistical returns [@ICM2020MadagascarAtlas; @Grandidier1885HistoirePhysique; @Escamps1858HistoireGeographie]. Within the `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$total_area_km2, 0L)` km² study domain bounded by geoBoundaries national polygons [@Runfola2020GeoBoundaries], one duplicate Wave-3 entry for Antananarivo was merged, retaining `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements across all ten sub-regions (`r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` observations).

## Site-Specific Population Estimation

Every entry holds a city-proper spatial scope (96 city-proper, 0 metro) anchored to surveyed enclosure hectares, compound counts, missionary estimates and official port or commune censuses [@Campbell1991ImperialMadagascar; @Larson2000HistoryMemory; @Allen1999SlavesFreedmen]. Tables 1 to 10 display linearly interpolated headcounts at five historical benchmarks (1100AD, 1400AD, 1700AD, 1810AD and 1890AD) alongside each settlement's observed peak population and date, marking eras outside a site's attested span with a hyphen (-).

# Testing and Validation

Across all `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements, rank-size regression on peak populations yields an upper-half (n=48) Zipf exponent of $q = 0,866$ ($R^2 = 0,9856$) and a full-sample slope of $q = 1,088$ ($R^2 = 0,8308$) (Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank}). All ten sub-regions contain multiple attested centres, ranging from 6 sites in Betsileo and Sakalava up to 17 communes and port towns across Mauritius, Réunion and Rodrigues, with zero duplicate aliases remaining after screening.

```{r fig3-ranksize, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig_03_rank_size.png",
  "Zipf rank-size curve across 96 island settlements (q = 0,87, R² = 0,99) and gridded sub-regional population densities in 1890AD.",
  "fig:settlements-rank",
  arg3_options = list(max_height = "0.38\\textheight")
)
```

# Results

## Kingdom of Imerina and Central Highlands

Table \ref{tab:sub-merina} documents `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["merina_central_highlands"]]), 0L)` settlements in central Madagascar and its eastern Merina corridor, led by Antananarivo (75k peak in 1817AD), Toamasina (10,2k), Ambohimanga (6,42k), Mahavelona (5,42k) and Alasora (4,12k) [@Raison1977PerceptionRealisation; @Campbell1991ImperialMadagascar; @Larson2000HistoryMemory].

```{r tab-merina, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["merina_central_highlands"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in the Kingdom of Imerina and Central Highlands (1100AD to 1890AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-merina")
)
```

## Portuguese Cabo Verde Archipelago

Table \ref{tab:sub-caboverde} lists `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["cabo_verde_atlantic"]]), 0L)` Cabo Verdean towns across the Sotavento and Barlavento islands, from early Ribeira Grande on Santiago (3,15k) and São Filipe on Fogo (3,24k) to Praia (4,65k), Ribeira Grande on Santo Antão (3,68k), Ribeira Brava (3,05k) and Mindelo (6,24k) [@Seibert2014CrioulizacaoCabo; @Keese2024BetweenLand; @Jung2015MigrationRemittances].

```{r tab-caboverde, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["cabo_verde_atlantic"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in the Portuguese Cabo Verde Archipelago (1100AD to 1890AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-caboverde")
)
```

## São Tomé, Príncipe and South Atlantic Islands

Table \ref{tab:sub-stp} presents `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["sao_tome_principe_st_helena"]]), 0L)` Gulf of Guinea and South Atlantic settlements, pairing São Tomé (6,85k), Santo António (2,35k), São João dos Angolares (1,42k) and Trindade (1,24k) with Jamestown (2,45k) and Longwood (640) on Saint Helena, Georgetown on Ascension (310) and Edinburgh of the Seven Seas on Tristan da Cunha (109) [@Fonju2021ToticPortuguese; @Berthet2016SaoTome].

```{r tab-stp, results='asis'}

  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["sao_tome_principe_st_helena"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in São Tomé, Príncipe and the South Atlantic Islands (1100AD to 1890AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-stp")
)
```

## Seychelles and Chagos Archipelago

Table \ref{tab:sub-seychelles} catalogues `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["seychelles_chagos_wio"]]), 0L)` settlements across the granitic Seychelles and Chagos copra stations: Victoria (6,24k), Grand'Anse on Praslin (1,18k), Anse Royale (1,12k) and La Digue (720) alongside East Point on Diego Garcia (428), Île du Coin in Peros Banhos (224) and Boddam in Salomon Islands (192).

```{r tab-seychelles, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["seychelles_chagos_wio"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in the Seychelles and Chagos Archipelago (1100AD to 1890AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:sub-seychelles")
)
```

# Limitations

Three caveats govern this gazetteer. First, 18 of the 96 settlements hold single-date observations (mostly 1878AD to 1895AD colonial surveys), so interpolated benchmark columns show a hyphen outside their attested span while reporting their full value in the peak column. Second, pre-colonial Malagasy and Comorian archaeological estimates carry wider uncertainty bounds than eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Mascarene or Portuguese enumerations [@ICM2020MadagascarAtlas; @Allen1999SlavesFreedmen]. Third, Seychelles and Chagos urban populations appear here in full even though those tiny island polygons register zero rural population on the coarse 5-arcminute regional raster.

# Conclusion

Together, the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements document the long transition from Austronesian-Bantu and Swahili-Shirazi coastal townlands to colonial sugar ports, coaling stations and unified highland capitals across ten island jurisdictions between 500BC and 1895AD.

# Appendix

## Sub-Regional Gazetteer Summary

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-summary} sums the individually assessed site counts and combined interpolated urban populations across all ten sub-regions from 1100AD to 1890AD.

```{r tab-appendix-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- zone_entries[[sid]]
  sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
    vals <- vapply(sub, function (e) {
      p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
      if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
    }, numeric(1))
    viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
  }, character(1)), bench_keys)
  data.frame(
    `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0(sub_by_id[[sid]]$name, " (", viscount_fmt_number(length(sub), 0L), ")"),
    `1100AD` = sums[["1100"]],
    `1400AD` = sums[["1400"]],
    `1700AD` = sums[["1700"]],
    `1810AD` = sums[["1810"]],
    `1890AD` = sums[["1890"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
tot_sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
  vals <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
    p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
    if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
  }, numeric(1))
  viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
}, character(1)), bench_keys)
tot_row <- data.frame(
  `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0("All Subregions (", viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L), ")"),
  `1100AD` = tot_sums[["1100"]],
  `1400AD` = tot_sums[["1400"]],
  `1700AD` = tot_sums[["1700"]],
  `1810AD` = tot_sums[["1810"]],
  `1890AD` = tot_sums[["1890"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(do.call(rbind, sum_rows), tot_row)
rownames(df_sum) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Individually assessed site counts and combined interpolated populations across ten sub-regions from 1100AD to 1890AD.",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:gazetteer-summary")
)
```
